Affenpinscher.physical_traits: Wiry black or dark coat, monkey-like facial appearance with a prominent chin and mustache, compact frame.
Affenpinscher.specialty: Originally bred as 17th-century kitchen and stable ratters; nicknamed the 'Monkey Terrier' (Affe = ape/monkey in German) due to its flat, primate-like facial expressions.
Affenpinscher.care_notes: Prone to brachycephalic airway syndrome; requires regular hand-stripping or grooming to maintain the wiry coat.

Afghan Hound.temperament: Aloof, independent, dignified, fiercely loyal once bonded
Afghan Hound.physical_traits: Flowing, fine-textured coat, tall slender build, distinct topknot, curved ring tail.
Afghan Hound.specialty: Capable of dramatic acceleration and agility across rocky mountain terrains; historically hunted leopards, gazelles, and hares by sight.
Afghan Hound.care_notes: Demands intensive coat grooming (several hours weekly) and secure running spaces due to high prey drive.

African Hunting Dog.physical_traits: Mottled tricolor coat (no two dogs have identical patterns), large rounded bat-like ears, four-toed paws (lacking dewclaws).
African Hunting Dog.specialty: Possesses one of the highest hunting success rates in the animal kingdom (up to 80%) via synchronized pack endurance coursing.
African Hunting Dog.care_notes: Not a domestic dog breed; strictly a protected wild species with complex social hierarchies.

Airedale.physical_traits: Largest of all terriers, dense wiry black-and-tan coat, long head, erect folded ears.
Airedale.specialty: Known as the 'King of Terriers'; served extensively in World War I as messenger and sentry dogs carrying crucial dispatches across battlefields.
Airedale.care_notes: High mental and physical stamina; needs regular vigorous runs and firm, varied obedience training.

American Staffordshire Terrier.physical_traits: Broad skull, heavy jaw, short glossy coat, powerful muscular frame.
American Staffordshire Terrier.specialty: Notable strength-to-weight ratio coupled with remarkable affinity for human companionship; distinguished from the APBT by AKC show conformation standards.
American Staffordshire Terrier.care_notes: Requires early socialization with other canines and robust interactive chew toys due to jaw strength.

Appenzeller.temperament: Energetic, vigilant, intelligent, suspicious of strangers
Appenzeller.physical_traits: Tricolor (black/havana brown with rust and white markings), compact muscular body, ring tail carried tightly over the back.
Appenzeller.specialty: Traditional Alpine cattle herder and drover capable of managing stock on steep, rocky gradients with relentless agility.
Appenzeller.care_notes: Demands an active, working lifestyle; will invent destructive jobs if left understimulated.

Australian Terrier.physical_traits: Rough, weather-resistant blue-and-tan or red coat with a distinct soft neck ruff and topknot; short-legged build.
Australian Terrier.specialty: The first native breed developed in Australia; bred to eradicate destructive vermin and small venomous snakes on outback stations.
Australian Terrier.care_notes: Strong hunting instinct; should be exercised on leash or within rodent-secure fencing.

Basenji.physical_traits: Wrinkled forehead, tightly curled tail, fine silky coat, prick ears.
Basenji.specialty: The famous 'barkless dog'; emits a yodel-like sound called a 'baroo' due to a flat laryngeal ventricle, and grooms itself meticulously like a feline.
Basenji.care_notes: Very low odor and minimal shedding, but extremely escape-prone and independent during recall.

Basset.physical_traits: Heavy-boned, elongated body, short bowed legs, loose skin folds, pendulous ears.
Basset.specialty: Second only to the Bloodhound in olfactory acuity; trailing scent low to the ground with oversized ears that sweep scents directly toward the nose.
Basset.care_notes: Prone to ear infections, bloat, and spinal strain; avoid excessive jumping off furniture.

Beagle.physical_traits: Compact, square-jawed, medium build, white-tipped tail (the 'flag' for high-grass visibility), tricolor or lemon-and-white coat.
Beagle.specialty: Exceptional pack-hunting scent abilities; widely deployed at international airports worldwide to detect contraband agricultural imports.
Beagle.care_notes: Can follow a scent trail for miles without heed; voice features a distinct musical three-way bay/howl.

Bedlington Terrier.physical_traits: Lamb-like silhouette, pear-shaped head with silky topknot, arched back, crisp non-shedding curly coat.
Bedlington Terrier.specialty: Bred to pursue badgers and rats in coal mines; possesses blistering coursing speed matching sighthounds when sprinting.
Bedlington Terrier.care_notes: Genetically predisposed to Copper Toxicosis (hepatic copper storage disease); coat requires scissor styling.

Bernese Mountain Dog.temperament: Gentle, calm, eager to please, loyal
Bernese Mountain Dog.physical_traits: Large, thick tricolor double coat (jet black, rich rust, pure white blaze), broad chest, expressive dark eyes.
Bernese Mountain Dog.specialty: All-around Alpine farm utility dog used for drafting heavy milk and cheese carts to market and watching farmsteads.
Bernese Mountain Dog.care_notes: Heat-sensitive with a relatively short average lifespan (6–8 years); heavy seasonal shedder.

Black-And-Tan Coonhound.physical_traits: Coal-black coat with rich tan points, long pendulous ears hanging well below the snout, deep chest.
Black-And-Tan Coonhound.specialty: Cold-nosed tracker capable of picking up faded scent trails that are days old to tree nocturnal raccoons and opossums.
Black-And-Tan Coonhound.care_notes: Requires significant scent enrichment; voice carries over miles via a booming, resonating bay.

Blenheim Spaniel.physical_traits: Chestnut-red patches on a pearly white ground; often exhibits the historic 'lozenge' thumbprint mark on top of the skull.
Blenheim Spaniel.specialty: Named after Blenheim Palace by the 1st Duke of Marlborough, who selected this specific color pattern for lap and field companions.
Blenheim Spaniel.care_notes: Prone to Mitral Valve Disease (MVD) and syringomyelia; requires regular heart screenings.

Bloodhound.temperament: Mild-mannered, relentless on a trail, sensitive, stubborn
Bloodhound.physical_traits: Massive loose skin folds, deep sunken eyes, exceedingly long drooping ears, powerful muscular build.
Bloodhound.specialty: Olfactory capability containing over 300 million scent receptors; trailing results are legally admissible in many courts of law.
Bloodhound.care_notes: Heavy drooler; requires daily cleaning of deep facial and ear wrinkles to prevent moisture dermatitis.

Bluetick.temperament: Bold, tenacious, deeply affectionate with its human pack
Bluetick.physical_traits: Dark blue coat pattern mottled with thick black ticking and tan points; athletic, square frame.
Bluetick.specialty: Cold-nosed trailing hound with exceptional focus, traditionally used to pursue nocturnal game, wild boar, and cougars.
Bluetick.care_notes: High exercise demands; will relentlessly bay at fence lines if it catches neighborhood scent lines.

Border Collie.physical_traits: Athletic, medium build, smooth or rough coat, intense piercing stare ('the eye').
Border Collie.specialty: Widely ranked as the most intelligent dog breed; controls sheep flocks with subtle body language and an intense psychological stare.
Border Collie.care_notes: Requires intensive mental work (agility, complex trick training, herding); easily develops neurotic behaviors if idle.

Border Terrier.physical_traits: Otter-like head shape, thick weather-hardy wiry coat, loose pelt, carrot-shaped tail.
Border Terrier.specialty: Bred to bolt foxes from underground burrows while possessing long enough legs to run alongside horses and foxhound packs.
Border Terrier.care_notes: Tough hide designed to resist thorns and bites; requires hand-stripping twice a year.

Borzoi.physical_traits: Long, narrow head, arched back, silky wavy coat, tall and lean greyhound-like chassis.
Borzoi.specialty: Bred by Russian Tsars and aristocracy for dramatic wolf hunts across the steppes, reaching top speeds of 35-40 mph.
Borzoi.care_notes: Sensitive to anesthesia; needs spacious indoor resting beds to protect lean joints.

Boston Bull.physical_traits: Distinct tuxedo-patterned coat (black, seal, or brindle with white), square head, large round dark eyes, erect ears.
Boston Bull.specialty: Dubbed 'The American Gentleman' for its dapper appearance and genial temperament; the official state dog of Massachusetts.
Boston Bull.care_notes: Brachycephalic; sensitive to temperature extremes and vigorous exertion in high humidity.

Bouvier Des Flandres.physical_traits: Heavy-boned, thick tousled double coat with beard and mustache, strong muscular jaw.
Bouvier Des Flandres.specialty: Original Flemish cattle drover and draft dog; later proved heroic in both World Wars as an ambulance and military search dog.
Bouvier Des Flandres.care_notes: Dense coat acts as a dirt magnet; requires substantial weekly brushing to prevent heavy matting.

Boxer.physical_traits: Square muscular build, undershot bite, tight smooth coat, high head carriage.
Boxer.specialty: Known for using its front paws extensively during play and self-defense, resembling a boxer spar; early guide dog and police pioneer.
Boxer.care_notes: High cancer and cardiomyopathy incidence; requires moderate exercise in temperate conditions.

Brabancon Griffon.physical_traits: Smooth short coat (unlike rough Griffons), pouty undershot jaw, large prominent human-like eyes.
Brabancon Griffon.specialty: Smooth-coated variety of the Brussels Griffon, valued for its comedic, expressive face and historical role catching stable rats.
Brabancon Griffon.care_notes: Prone to eye abrasions and heat stress due to shallow orbits and short nasal passages.

Briard.physical_traits: Long coarse coat parted down the middle, beard, eyebrows, distinctive double dewclaws on each hind leg.
Briard.specialty: Centuries-old flock sentinel and herder; historical records document Napoleon, Lafayette, and Thomas Jefferson admiring their devotion.
Briard.care_notes: Double dewclaws are a breed standard requirement and must be monitored for snagging; heavy coat care.

Brittany Spaniel.physical_traits: Compact, leggy bird dog with an orange/liver and white coat, naturally tailless or docked short.
Brittany Spaniel.specialty: Dual-purpose pointing and retrieving dog that works closer to the foot hunter than traditional pointers, possessing exceptional scent tracking.
Brittany Spaniel.care_notes: Responds poorly to harsh discipline; requires gentle, positive training combined with high-cadence field workouts.

Bull Mastiff.physical_traits: Massive bone structure, broad wrinkled skull, dark mask, short dense fawn/red/brindle coat.
Bull Mastiff.specialty: The 'Gamekeeper's Night Dog'; engineered (60% Mastiff, 40% Bulldog) to silently stalk, pin, and hold poachers without mauling them.
Bull Mastiff.care_notes: Needs firm leadership from puppyhood; natural guardian that rarely barks unless a real threat is present.

Cairn.physical_traits: Harsh weather-resistant shaggy coat, wide-set eyes, upright pointed ears, compact sturdy stance.
Cairn.specialty: Bred to crawl deep into cairns (stone piles) to dispatch otters, badgers, and foxes; famously depicted by 'Toto' in The Wizard of Oz.
Cairn.care_notes: Compulsive digger; needs safe digging pits or outlets to satisfy root-hunting instincts.

Cardigan.physical_traits: Low-slung silhouette, prominent arched fox-like brush tail, rounded large bat ears, slightly curved front legs.
Cardigan.specialty: Dating back over 3,000 years with Celtic settlers; nips cattle heels and stays low to duck swinging kicks from dairy cows.
Cardigan.care_notes: Long spine requires monitoring weight to prevent intervertebral disc disease (IVDD).

Chesapeake Bay Retriever.physical_traits: Harsh, oily, wavy outer coat with a dense woolly undercoat; amber eyes; colors camouflage with dead grass/sedges.
Chesapeake Bay Retriever.specialty: Known to retrieve up to 200 ducks a day out of freezing, ice-choked Chesapeake waters; uniquely protective among sporting breeds.
Chesapeake Bay Retriever.care_notes: Natural coat oils smell distinctly of musk and should not be stripped with excessive shampooing.

Chihuahua.physical_traits: Smallest dog breed in the world; apple dome skull, luminous round eyes, large flaring ears.
Chihuahua.specialty: Descended from the ancient Toltec Techichi; regarded as sacred companion animals with spiritual healing roles.
Chihuahua.care_notes: Prone to luxating patellas, hypoglycemia in youth, and cold weather tremors; requires warm clothing in winter.

Chow.physical_traits: Lion-like ruff, straight hocks producing a stilted gait, distinctive blue-black tongue, deep-set almond eyes.
Chow.specialty: Versatile imperial hunting, guarding, and sledding canine dating back to the Han Dynasty; rare blue-black tongue shared only with the Shar-Pei.
Chow.care_notes: Strict early socialization required; limited peripheral vision due to deep-set eyes means they dislike being startled.

Clumber.physical_traits: Heaviest of the spaniel breeds; massive head, heavy bone, low chassis, thick lemon/orange-marked white coat.
Clumber.specialty: Built for pushing through dense, impenetrable brambles to flush game birds for aristocratic shooting parties.
Clumber.care_notes: Prone to drooling, snoring, and joint strain; exercise should be steady rather than high-impact.

Cocker Spaniel.temperament: Gentle, playful, happy, eager to please
Cocker Spaniel.physical_traits: Lush, feathered silky coat, rounded skull, soft pleading expression, long pendant ears.
Cocker Spaniel.specialty: Historically specialized in flushing the woodcock (source of the name 'Cocker'); excels in both fieldwork and obedience rings.
Cocker Spaniel.care_notes: Ears require regular cleaning to avoid yeast/bacterial infections; coat requires frequent brushing.

Collie.physical_traits: Wedge-shaped refined head, semi-prick ears, available in Rough (long luxurious mane) and Smooth varieties.
Collie.specialty: Legendary sheep-herding precision in rugged Scottish highlands; popularized worldwide for heroic loyalty by Albert Payson Terhune and 'Lassie'.
Collie.care_notes: High frequency of the MDR1 gene mutation, making them hypersensitive to specific antiparasitic drugs like ivermectin.

Curly-Coated Retriever.physical_traits: Solid mass of crisp, small, tight water-repellent curls covering the body except the face; deep chestnut or black.
Curly-Coated Retriever.specialty: One of the oldest retriever breeds; renowned for swimming through icy duck marshes and drying remarkably fast.
Curly-Coated Retriever.care_notes: Brushing frizzes the coat; needs air-drying and occasional water-misting to reform the distinct curls.

Dandie Dinmont.physical_traits: Long body with an arched weasel-like top-line, very short legs, silken powder-puff topknot, large expressive eyes.
Dandie Dinmont.specialty: The only breed named after a fictional character (from Sir Walter Scott's novel *Guy Mannering*); specialized in hunting otters and badgers.
Dandie Dinmont.care_notes: Spinal care is essential; avoid stairs and excess jumping to protect the long back.

Dhole.physical_traits: Rusty-red coat, dark bushy tail, rounded ears, lacks the third lower molar tooth compared to domestic dogs.
Dhole.specialty: Communicates through distinct whistles and clucks so unique they can coordinate complex pack ambushes out of sight in thick jungle.
Dhole.care_notes: Endangered wild apex predator; completely unsuited to domestication.

Dingo.physical_traits: Sandy-yellow to red coat with white paws and tail tip, flexible wrists, highly mobile head rotating nearly 180 degrees.
Dingo.specialty: Apex land predator of the Australian continent; introduced thousands of years ago, maintaining wild ecological equilibrium.
Dingo.care_notes: Wild species; possess specialized climbing and jumping abilities capable of scaling 6-foot fences easily.

Doberman.physical_traits: Sleek, muscular, compact wedge body, clean lines, rust markings on black, red, blue, or fawn.
Doberman.specialty: Created by tax collector Louis Dobermann for personal defense; serves as a premier protection, sentry, and military canine.
Doberman.care_notes: Genetically predisposed to Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM) and von Willebrand's Disease; needs extensive early socialization.

English Foxhound.physical_traits: Clean, sturdy bone structure, hard short coat, level back, hound-marked in black, white, and tan.
English Foxhound.specialty: Engineered for centuries to course foxes alongside mounted hunters over miles of country without slowing down.
English Foxhound.care_notes: Thrives best in multi-dog households or packs; rarely content as a purely sedentary house dog.

English Setter.physical_traits: Graceful carriage, long feathered coat with unique speckled patterns called 'belton' (blue, orange, tricolor).
English Setter.specialty: The 'Gentleman of the Dog World'; crouches ('sets') silently upon locating game birds to allow nets or shooters to approach.
English Setter.care_notes: Prone to congenital deafness and hip dysplasia; regular brushing preserves the long feathering.

English Springer.temperament: Friendly, playful, eager to work, obedient
English Springer.physical_traits: Medium build, fringed ears, muscular legs, weather-resistant coat with white and liver or black patches.
English Springer.specialty: Master of flushing ('springing') upland game birds from dense underbrush into flight for the hunter.
English Springer.care_notes: Subdivided into distinct Field and Show lines; Field lines have intense physical drives and require heavy exercise.

Entlebucher.physical_traits: Smallest Swiss Mountain Dog; compact, heavy-muscled, short tricolor coat, wedge-shaped head.
Entlebucher.specialty: High-speed cattle driver nicknamed the 'Laufer' (runner); operates through heel-nipping and rapid changes of direction.
Entlebucher.care_notes: Can become overly vocal and protective if not trained with firm structure from early months.

Eskimo Dog.physical_traits: Pure white or biscuit-cream double coat, black points (nose, lips, eye rims), plumed tail curved over the back.
Eskimo Dog.specialty: Gained fame in early 20th-century traveling circuses (such as Barnum & Bailey) as acrobatic, tightrope-walking performance canines.
Eskimo Dog.care_notes: Heavy seasonal shedding requires frequent deshedding brush routines; alert barker.

Flat-Coated Retriever.physical_traits: Seamless, lustrous flat coat in solid black or liver; long, clean one-piece head structure.
Flat-Coated Retriever.specialty: The 'Peter Pan' of gun dogs; maintains energetic puppy-like enthusiasm well into adulthood while excelling in water bird work.
Flat-Coated Retriever.care_notes: Higher statistical incidence of histiocytic sarcomas and other cancers compared to other sporting breeds.

French Bulldog.physical_traits: Compact, heavy-boned body, distinct upright 'bat ears', flat face with wrinkles, short smooth coat.
French Bulldog.specialty: Bred down from toy bulldogs by Nottingham lace-makers who relocated to Paris; excellent low-barking apartment companion.
French Bulldog.care_notes: Strictly brachycephalic; cannot swim due to dense front-heavy physiology; sensitive to overheating.

German Shepherd.physical_traits: Erect ears, noble carriage, strong back, double coat in black and tan, sable, or solid black.
German Shepherd.specialty: Standardized by Max von Stephanitz; represents the gold standard in military, police, detection, and personal defense work globally.
German Shepherd.care_notes: Susceptible to hip and elbow dysplasia, degenerative myelopathy, and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI).

German Short-Haired Pointer.physical_traits: Streamlined athletic build, liver or liver-and-white ticked short coat, broad muzzle, docked tail.
German Short-Haired Pointer.specialty: All-in-one hunting dog engineered to point, track, and retrieve game on land or water across any terrain.
German Short-Haired Pointer.care_notes: Extreme exercise requirements; needs hours of open-field running or scent tracking to remain calm indoors.

Giant Schnauzer.physical_traits: Large, powerfully built frame, harsh wiry dense coat with thick beard and dramatic eyebrows; solid black or pepper-and-salt.
Giant Schnauzer.specialty: Bred up from standard schnauzers and Great Danes to drive cattle and guard Bavarian breweries and rail yards.
Giant Schnauzer.care_notes: Requires strong, confident leadership and routine hand-stripping to maintain proper harsh coat texture.

Golden Retriever.temperament: Friendly, reliable, patient, eager to please
Golden Retriever.physical_traits: Water-repellent golden or cream coat with feathery fringes, broad skull, friendly dark eyes.
Golden Retriever.specialty: Bred by Lord Tweedmouth at Guisachan to retrieve wildfowl undamaged ('soft mouth'); premier guide dog and search canine.
Golden Retriever.care_notes: High cancer rates; requires regular cardiovascular exercise and daily brush-outs during shedding seasons.

Gordon Setter.physical_traits: Heaviest of the setters; glistening coal-black coat with rich mahogany or chestnut spots, aristocratic head.
Gordon Setter.specialty: Developed by the 4th Duke of Gordon; a methodical bird hunter capable of working grueling hours in cold Scottish weather.
Gordon Setter.care_notes: Slower to mature mentally than other sporting breeds; deeply devoted to one family.

Great Dane.physical_traits: Colossal height, square muscular frame, long narrow head, short smooth coat.
Great Dane.specialty: Historically bred to bring down massive European wild boars; holds multiple world records for the tallest domestic dogs.
Great Dane.care_notes: Prone to gastric dilatation-volvulus (bloat/torsion); prophylactic gastropexy is frequently recommended.

Great Pyrenees.physical_traits: Weatherproof thick white double coat, dark soulful eyes, double dewclaws on rear legs.
Great Pyrenees.specialty: Livestock guardian bred to deter wolves and bears; operates autonomously without human direction, often active at night.
Great Pyrenees.care_notes: Deep, booming guardian bark; independent nature makes standard leash obedience training a test of patience.

Greater Swiss Mountain Dog.physical_traits: Heavy-boned, short dense tricolor coat, broad head, muscular shoulders.
Greater Swiss Mountain Dog.specialty: The 'poor man's horse' of Switzerland; excelled in heavy freight hauling, draft work, and livestock driving.
Greater Swiss Mountain Dog.care_notes: Slow physical and mental maturation (up to 3 years); vulnerable to bloat and joint wear from excessive early strain.

Groenendael.physical_traits: Solid pitch-black long coat with a prominent collarette around the neck; erect triangular ears.
Groenendael.specialty: The black variety of the Belgian Shepherd; excelled as a World War I trench patrol dog, tracking sentry, and tracker.
Groenendael.care_notes: Can become overly sensitive if trained with harsh corrections; needs engaging, positive-reinforcement agility work.

Ibizan Hound.physical_traits: Lean chassis, large upright ears, flesh-colored nose and amber eyes, smooth or wire red-and-white coat.
Ibizan Hound.specialty: Hunts rabbits using sight, scent, and acute hearing; capable of springing 5 to 6 feet vertically from a dead standstill.
Ibizan Hound.care_notes: Very high prey drive; requires exceptionally tall fencing (at least 6 feet) to contain.

Irish Setter.physical_traits: Flowing, glossy rich chestnut or mahogany-red coat, lean muzzle, long feathery tail.
Irish Setter.specialty: Field bird dog known for sweeping, rapid ground hunting; renowned for its show-ring glamour and boundless good cheer.
Irish Setter.care_notes: Requires substantial aerobic workouts daily to prevent hyperactive or restless home behavior.

Irish Terrier.temperament: Courageous, spirited, tender with family, feisty
Irish Terrier.physical_traits: Dense, wiry bright-red coat, racy outline, beard, folded V-shaped ears.
Irish Terrier.specialty: Nicknamed 'the Daredevil'; served with distinction in World War I trenches as heroic messengers amidst artillery fire.
Irish Terrier.care_notes: High dog-on-dog reactivity if unsocialized; strong vermin drive makes secure leashing essential.

Irish Water Spaniel.physical_traits: Crisply curled liver-purple coat, distinctive topknot of loose curls, hairless smooth 'rat tail'.
Irish Water Spaniel.specialty: The tallest spaniel breed; bred to retrieve game from rough, cold Atlantic coastal waters and bogs.
Irish Water Spaniel.care_notes: Low-shedding coat requires regular scissoring and detangling; water-loving and needs regular swimming outlets.

Irish Wolfhound.physical_traits: The tallest of all AKC breeds; rough wiry grey/brindle coat, muscular galloping physique, long curved tail.
Irish Wolfhound.specialty: Ancient sighthound historically used to hunt down the extinct Irish giant elk and clear the countryside of wolves.
Irish Wolfhound.care_notes: Heartbreakingly brief lifespan (6–8 years); prone to osteosarcoma, heart disease, and gastric torsion.

Italian Greyhound.physical_traits: Miniature Greyhound silhouette; fragile slender bones, glossy short coat, tucked abdomen.
Italian Greyhound.specialty: Renaissance lap companion of European royalty; possesses true double-suspension gallop mechanics reaching speeds over 25 mph.
Italian Greyhound.care_notes: Prone to leg fractures from jumping off heights during youth; highly sensitive to cold temperatures and rain.

Japanese Spaniel.physical_traits: Under-jaw undershot bite, feathered tail curved over back, wide-set dark eyes with white visible in corners ('astonished look').
Japanese Spaniel.specialty: Also known as the Japanese Chin; bred for imperial Japanese palaces; known for the 'Chin spin' (rapid dancing pirouettes).
Japanese Spaniel.care_notes: Grooms itself with paws like a cat; prone to heat exhaustion and corneal abrasions.

Keeshond.physical_traits: Plush silver-and-black coat with lion-like ruff, curled tail, distinct dark 'spectacles' markings around eyes.
Keeshond.specialty: Historic watchdog of Dutch canal barges; became the symbol of the Dutch Patriot political party in the 18th century.
Keeshond.care_notes: Dense double coat sheds heavily in seasonal cycles; requires thorough undercoat raking without shaving.

Kelpie.physical_traits: Compact, athletic, prick ears, short weather-resistant double coat in black, red, fawn, or chocolate.
Kelpie.specialty: Engineered to manage thousands of sheep across blistering Australian outback paddocks; famous for running across the backs of tightly packed sheep.
Kelpie.care_notes: Unsuitable as an ordinary apartment pet; requires miles of daily running and complex stock herding work.

Kerry Blue Terrier.physical_traits: Soft, wavy, non-shedding coat that transitions from jet-black at birth to slate blue-gray by adulthood; full beard.
Kerry Blue Terrier.specialty: All-around Irish farm utility dog used for herding cattle, retrieving water birds, and controlling heavy vermin.
Kerry Blue Terrier.care_notes: Coat requires dedicated scissor styling; strong prey drive toward strange cats and smaller animals.

Komondor.physical_traits: Large muscular frame covered completely in dense, white, felted cords resembling a floor mop.
Komondor.specialty: Flock guardian that blends invisibly among sheep until wolves or bears attack; cords act as armor against carnivore bites.
Komondor.care_notes: Cords must be washed and separated by hand; drying a fully corded adult coat can take 24–48 hours.

Kuvasz.temperament: Regal, fiercely loyal, patient, suspicious of outsiders
Kuvasz.physical_traits: Large, dense double coat of wavy pure white or ivory hair, dark almond-shaped eyes, muscular build.
Kuvasz.specialty: Royal guard canine of King Matthias Corvinus in the 15th century; highly protective guardian of sheep and horses against predators.
Kuvasz.care_notes: Needs extensive socialization starting in early puppyhood to keep its intense guarding instincts manageable.

Labrador Retriever.temperament: Outgoing, even-tempered, eager to please, loving
Labrador Retriever.physical_traits: Dense water-repellent double coat, distinct broad 'otter tail', kind eyes, strong neck and shoulders.
Labrador Retriever.specialty: Aided Newfoundland fishermen hauling nets in icy waters; world's leading breed for assistance, service, guide, and detection work.
Labrador Retriever.care_notes: Prone to obesity and hip/elbow dysplasia; needs careful calorie management and regular swimming/fetching.

Lakeland Terrier.physical_traits: Narrow-bodied, harsh wiry coat, folded ears, upright tail; bearded muzzle.
Lakeland Terrier.specialty: Bred to protect sheep flocks by tracking and pursuing foxes into steep, narrow rocky dens inaccessible to other dogs.
Lakeland Terrier.care_notes: Wired coat requires hand-stripping; thrives on high-energy play and agility challenges.

Leonberg.physical_traits: Giant size, lion-like mane around neck and chest, black facial mask, water-resistant double coat.
Leonberg.specialty: Bred by Heinrich Essig to mimic the lion on the town crest of Leonberg; combines Newfoundland, Saint Bernard, and Great Pyrenees bloodlines.
Leonberg.care_notes: Major drooler and shedder; requires huge living spaces and consistent low-impact exercise during growth periods.

Lhasa.temperament: Independent, dignified, watchful, affectionate with family
Lhasa.physical_traits: Heavy, straight, floor-length parted coat, dark eyes covered by hair, plumed tail carried high over the back.
Lhasa.specialty: The 'Bark Lion Sentinel Dog' (Abso Seng Kye) of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, sounding the alarm if intruders breached the outer gates.
Lhasa.care_notes: Coat requires daily combing to prevent mats, or a practical puppy clip; naturally aloof with strangers.

Malamute.physical_traits: Heavy-boned, thick coarse double coat, cap-and-mask face markings, plumed tail carried over spine.
Malamute.specialty: Developed by the Mahlemut Inuit tribe for freighting heavy cargo sleds over extreme Arctic distances (freight train of the north).
Malamute.care_notes: High escape drive; will dig out under fences; howls rather than barks; sheds profusely in seasonal blowouts.

Malinois.physical_traits: Fawn to mahogany coat with black tips, black mask and ears, athletic square build.
Malinois.specialty: The preferred breed for modern elite counter-terrorism military units (Navy SEALs) and SWAT teams due to unmatched drive and agility.
Malinois.care_notes: Not suitable for novice dog owners; requires hours of high-intensity operational tasks and daily training.

Maltese Dog.physical_traits: Pure white, silky, floor-length coat without undercoat, black button nose, dark expressive eyes.
Maltese Dog.specialty: Cherished by ancient Roman, Greek, and Egyptian royalty as the ultimate aristocratic lap companion for millennia.
Maltese Dog.care_notes: Prone to tear staining under the eyes; requires daily coat maintenance to avoid mats.

Mexican Hairless.physical_traits: Available in Hairless (tough smooth skin) and Coated varieties; large upright ears, almond eyes.
Mexican Hairless.specialty: The Xoloitzcuintli was considered a sacred guide of souls to the Aztec underworld (Mictlan); radiates notable surface body heat.
Mexican Hairless.care_notes: Hairless skin requires sunscreen in high UV environments and gentle moisturizers to prevent dry skin.

Miniature Pinscher.physical_traits: Sleek muscular frame, high-stepping 'hackney' gait, smooth short coat in solid red, black-and-rust, or chocolate.
Miniature Pinscher.specialty: Nicknamed 'King of Toys'; despite looking like a mini Doberman, it is an older independent breed developed to kill barn rats.
Miniature Pinscher.care_notes: Skilled escape artist; can easily slip through narrow fence gaps; requires secure harness walking.

Miniature Poodle.physical_traits: Hypoallergenic curly dense coat, refined muzzle, square athletic body.
Miniature Poodle.specialty: Excels in agility, scent-work, and trick performance; scaled down from the Standard Poodle to hunt truffles across European woodlands.
Miniature Poodle.care_notes: Demands professional coat clipping every 4 to 6 weeks; needs regular mental enrichment.

Miniature Schnauzer.physical_traits: Wiry coat in salt-and-pepper, black-and-silver, or solid black; trademark bushy beard and eyebrows.
Miniature Schnauzer.specialty: The only terrier breed with zero British ancestry; bred to patrol German farms and clear out vermin.
Miniature Schnauzer.care_notes: Predisposed to hyperlipidemia and pancreatitis; requires a strictly controlled, low-fat diet.

Newfoundland.physical_traits: Massive frame, water-resistant oily double coat, webbed feet, deep chest.
Newfoundland.specialty: Lifesaving water rescue dog with lung capacity and strength to pull drowning victims and capsized boats ashore in stormy seas.
Newfoundland.care_notes: Heavy drooler and shedder; vulnerable to heat stroke and joint dysplasia.

Norfolk Terrier.physical_traits: Compact, short-legged, wiry coat, drop ears folded neatly forward.
Norfolk Terrier.specialty: One of the smallest working terriers; hunted rats in packs and bolted foxes from underground dens; differentiated from the Norwich by dropped ears.
Norfolk Terrier.care_notes: Needs hand-stripping to preserve coat weather-resistance; strong chase instinct for neighborhood squirrels.

Norwegian Elkhound.physical_traits: Thick silver-gray spitz coat with black tipping, curled tail held tight over back, erect pointed ears.
Norwegian Elkhound.specialty: Viking hound bred to track and hold giant moose (elk) and brown bears at bay using agile footwork and a continuous, barking cadence.
Norwegian Elkhound.care_notes: High barking frequency; sheds undercoat heavily during seasonal transitions.

Norwich Terrier.physical_traits: Compact, wire-haired, short-legged, erect pointed ears ('Norwich prick, Norfolk drop').
Norwich Terrier.specialty: Historically popular among Cambridge University students as a fashionable dorm rat-catcher and faithful companion.
Norwich Terrier.care_notes: Susceptible to Upper Airway Syndrome (UAS); benefits from hand-stripped grooming.

Old English Sheepdog.physical_traits: Profuse shaggy gray-and-white coat covering eyes, tailless or docked ('Bobtail'), distinctive lumbering, bear-like gait.
Old English Sheepdog.specialty: Drover dog that pushed cattle and sheep from pasture to Smithfield market; historically exempt from dog taxes due to their docked working tails.
Old English Sheepdog.care_notes: Intensive grooming commitment (multiple hours weekly) to prevent severe matting at the skin level.

Otterhound.physical_traits: Large rough-coated hound, webbed feet, oily waterproof coat, long folded ears, deep resonant voice.
Otterhound.specialty: Bred to track river otters in fast-flowing currents; one of the rarest breeds in the world with fewer than 1,000 specimens globally.
Otterhound.care_notes: Loves muddy water; large beard requires drying after drinking to avoid fungal skin conditions.

Papillon.physical_traits: Wing-like erect fringed ears resembling butterfly wings (papillon is French for butterfly), fine silky coat, plumed tail.
Papillon.specialty: Consistently ranked as the most intelligent toy breed; routinely outperforms larger breeds in international agility and trick trials.
Papillon.care_notes: Delicate leg bones in youth; low-maintenance coat despite its glamorous appearance as it lacks an undercoat.

Pekinese.physical_traits: Lion's mane ruff, flattened face, bowed front legs creating a distinct rolling gait, long feathering.
Pekinese.specialty: Sacred lap dog of the Chinese imperial court; according to legend, created by the Buddha shrinking a lion while retaining its brave heart.
Pekinese.care_notes: Brachycephalic; strict avoidance of hot environments; facial folds need daily hygienic cleaning.

Pembroke.physical_traits: Low-set, pointed prick ears, naturally bobbed or docked tail, foxy face, weather-hardy double coat.
Pembroke.specialty: Beloved royal companions of Queen Elizabeth II; works cattle by nipping heels and ducking low under kicking hooves.
Pembroke.care_notes: Prone to intervertebral disc disease (IVDD) and obesity; jump heights from sofas or beds must be managed.

Pomeranian.physical_traits: Fluffy standout double coat, fox-like expression, heavily plumed tail arching flat over the back, tiny prick ears.
Pomeranian.specialty: Miniaturized from larger Arctic sled dogs (Spitz); championed and popularized across Europe by Queen Victoria.
Pomeranian.care_notes: Prone to collapsing trachea and luxating patellas; use a harness rather than a neck collar on walks.

Pug.physical_traits: Square cobby body, deep wrinkles on flat face, curled tail (ideally a double curl), velvety black mask.
Pug.specialty: Treasured companion of Chinese emperors and later the Dutch House of Orange; celebrated under the motto 'Multum in Parvo' (much in little).
Pug.care_notes: Prone to heat exhaustion, corneal ulcers, and obesity; facial wrinkles must be kept dry.

Redbone.physical_traits: Gleaming solid rich red coat, athletic hound build, soulful pleading eyes, clean jawline.
Redbone.specialty: Bred to tree raccoons, bears, and cougars across Southern swamps and forests; popularized by the classic novel *Where the Red Fern Grows*.
Redbone.care_notes: Needs scent-focused enrichment; possesses a sweet nature indoors but turns single-minded on animal scent trails.

Rhodesian Ridgeback.physical_traits: Athletic muscular frame, wheaten color coat, distinct backward-growing ridge of hair along the spine.
Rhodesian Ridgeback.specialty: Bred to harass, corner, and bay lions for hunters without engaging in direct conflict; highly resistant to heat and tick-borne diseases.
Rhodesian Ridgeback.care_notes: Strong-willed; requires early guidance and consistent boundaries without harsh handling.

Rottweiler.physical_traits: Robust, muscular frame, broad skull, black coat with distinct rich rust-mahogany markings.
Rottweiler.specialty: Descended from Roman drover dogs; pulled butcher carts and guarded money pouches tied to their necks in the market town of Rottweil.
Rottweiler.care_notes: Needs rigorous early socialization and obedience training; excels at carting, tracking, and protection work.

Saint Bernard.physical_traits: Massive head, furrowed brow, dark mask, immense muscular body, smooth or rough dense coat.
Saint Bernard.specialty: Credited with saving over 2,000 travelers stranded in blizzards at the Great St. Bernard Pass hospice over several centuries.
Saint Bernard.care_notes: Heavy drooler; requires cold indoor areas; joints must be protected from heavy impact during rapid early growth.

Saluki.physical_traits: Symmetrical, deep-chested, silky feathering on ears and tail, smooth sleek body, remarkable grace.
Saluki.specialty: One of the oldest documented dog breeds, depicted in Egyptian tombs; hunted gazelles across open desert at speeds up to 42 mph.
Saluki.care_notes: Extremely low body fat makes them sensitive to hard sleeping surfaces and anesthesia; high prey drive.

Samoyed.physical_traits: Thick weather-resistant white coat, upturned black lips forming the famous 'Sammy smile', dark almond eyes.
Samoyed.specialty: Bred by nomadic Samoyedic reindeer herders to pull sleds, herd reindeer, and sleep directly with family members to provide radiant warmth.
Samoyed.care_notes: Upturned mouth corners prevent drool from freezing into icicles on its face; requires daily brushing to prevent mats.

Schipperke.physical_traits: Fox-like face, solid black coat with a thick neck ruff and culottes (hind leg hair), naturally tailless or docked.
Schipperke.specialty: The 'Little Captain' (Schip = boat) of Flemish canal barges; served as an uncompromising watchdog and ratter on boat decks.
Schipperke.care_notes: High energy packed in a small body; known as 'the black devil' due to its curious, mischievous ingenuity.

Scotch Terrier.physical_traits: Short legs, compact muscular body, prominent beard, pointed upright ears, dense wiry outer coat.
Scotch Terrier.specialty: Nicknamed 'The Diehard' for fearless perseverance against badgers and foxes; famous White House resident under FDR (Fala).
Scotch Terrier.care_notes: Poor swimmers due to heavy bones and short legs; susceptible to 'Scottie Cramp' during periods of high excitement.

Scottish Deerhound.physical_traits: Towering stature, rough weather-hardy gray wiry coat, deep chest, tapering tail.
Scottish Deerhound.specialty: The royal coursing hound of the Scottish Highlands, specially bred to run down and dispatch 250-pound red deer.
Scottish Deerhound.care_notes: Calm couch potato indoors, but needs a safe, fenced field to stretch into a full sprint regularly.

Sealyham Terrier.physical_traits: Low-slung, sturdy, dense all-white wiry coat, fall of hair covering forehead, strong jaw.
Sealyham Terrier.specialty: Developed by Captain John Edwardes to dispatch badgers and otters; once Hollywood's favorite breed (Alfred Hitchcock, Cary Grant).
Sealyham Terrier.care_notes: Much calmer indoors than many other terriers; beard requires frequent washing and drying.

Shetland Sheepdog.physical_traits: Miniature rough Collie silhouette; long wedge-shaped head, semi-pricked ears, rich double coat with heavy mane.
Shetland Sheepdog.specialty: Hardy island herder adapted to manage Shetland sheep, poultry, and miniature livestock in harsh, windy conditions.
Shetland Sheepdog.care_notes: Sensitive to vocal tones; excitable barker that requires early counter-conditioning; carries the MDR1 gene mutation risk.

Shih-Tzu.physical_traits: Flowing double coat, pushed-in nose, warm dark eyes, plumed tail carried neatly over back.
Shih-Tzu.specialty: The 'Chrysanthemum Dog' (facial hair grows outwards in all directions like flower petals); exclusively pampered lap dog of Ming and Qing dynasties.
Shih-Tzu.care_notes: Heat-sensitive; requires daily topknot grooming or hair clipping to prevent eye irritation.

Siberian Husky.physical_traits: Medium build, striking blue or bi-colored almond eyes, dense double coat, bushy fox-brush tail.
Siberian Husky.specialty: Bred by the Chukchi people for high-speed endurance hauling over frozen tundra; historic hero of the 1925 Nome Serum Run.
Siberian Husky.care_notes: Famous escape artists and howlers; possesses minimal territorial instinct, making them ineffective guard dogs.

Silky Terrier.physical_traits: Fine, glossy, parted blue-and-tan coat that does not touch the floor; wedge head, erect V-shaped ears.
Silky Terrier.specialty: Bred in Australia by crossing Yorkshire Terriers with Australian Terriers to create an urban vermin hunter and companion.
Silky Terrier.care_notes: True terrier prey drive despite toy stature; coat requires regular brushing to avoid painful tangles.

Soft-Coated Wheaten Terrier.physical_traits: Single coat of soft, wavy, warm wheaten silk; rectangular body, peppy tail carriage.
Soft-Coated Wheaten Terrier.specialty: All-purpose Irish farm dog; famously greets owners with the energetic, full-body 'Wheaten Greetin' leap.
Soft-Coated Wheaten Terrier.care_notes: Prone to protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) and nephropathy (PLN); coat requires daily detangling to prevent matting.

Staffordshire Bullterrier.temperament: Affectionate, courageous, playful, gentle with humans
Staffordshire Bullterrier.physical_traits: Short, muscular, broad skull, pronounced cheek muscles, wide chest, smooth tight coat.
Staffordshire Bullterrier.specialty: Nicknamed the 'Nanny Dog' in Britain for its patient, affectionate, and protective bond with children.
Staffordshire Bullterrier.care_notes: Requires strong chew toys due to jaw strength; requires early canine socialization to mitigate intra-species friction.

Standard Poodle.temperament: Brilliant, athletic, proud, eager to please
Standard Poodle.physical_traits: Dense curly non-shedding coat, square build, elegant carriage, long straight muzzle.
Standard Poodle.specialty: Originally a water retrieval dog (Pudelhund); the classic show clips were practical cuts to keep joints warm in freezing water while shedding drag.
Standard Poodle.care_notes: Ranks among the smartest breeds; thrives on advanced obedience, duck retrieving, and agility.

Standard Schnauzer.physical_traits: Square, robust build, harsh salt-and-pepper or solid black wiry coat with thick eyebrows and mustache.
Standard Schnauzer.specialty: The prototype schnauzer depicted in paintings by Rembrandt and Dürer; served as an all-around stable ratter and coach watchdog.
Standard Schnauzer.care_notes: Highly intelligent with an independent streak; requires mentally challenging training tasks.

Sussex Spaniel.temperament: Calm, cheerful, deliberate, vocal on trail
Sussex Spaniel.physical_traits: Low-slung body, massive bone, rich golden-liver coat, wide head with somber expression.
Sussex Spaniel.specialty: One of the few spaniels that bays ('gives tongue') while tracking hidden game through thick clay and dense underbrush.
Sussex Spaniel.care_notes: Prone to weight gain; needs moderate, consistent daily exercise and regular ear canal hygiene.

Tibetan Mastiff.physical_traits: Imposing giant frame, massive lion-like mane, deep-set eyes, heavy tail curled over back.
Tibetan Mastiff.specialty: Ancient Himalayan guardian of nomadic camps, livestock, and isolated monasteries; operates with nocturnal vigilance.
Tibetan Mastiff.care_notes: Not a standard domestic companion; fiercely territorial and requires dedicated, experienced handling.

Tibetan Terrier.physical_traits: Square body, profuse double coat covering eyes, unique flat wide 'snowshoe' round paws.
Tibetan Terrier.specialty: The 'Holy Dog of Tibet'; kept as good-luck charms in Buddhist monasteries; unique snowshoe feet provide traction on snowy precipices.
Tibetan Terrier.care_notes: Not a true terrier; demands careful line-brushing down to the skin several times a week.

Toy Poodle.physical_traits: Stands under 10 inches at the shoulder; curly dense coat, light springy gait, dark oval eyes.
Toy Poodle.specialty: Bred down as luxury companions for 18th-century French nobility; retains the full problem-solving intellect of larger poodles.
Toy Poodle.care_notes: Prone to dental tartar accumulation and luxating patellas; requires regular teeth brushing.

Toy Terrier.physical_traits: Sleek, ebony-black coat with defined chestnut-tan markings, candle-flame ears, delicate arched topline.
Toy Terrier.specialty: The English Toy Terrier (Black & Tan) was engineered to compete in 19th-century Victorian rat-pit gaming contests.
Toy Terrier.care_notes: Sensitive to winter chills; requires sweaters in cold weather and gentle handling around larger pets.

Vizsla.physical_traits: Sleek golden-rust coat, self-colored nose and nails, amber eyes, lean athletic build.
Vizsla.specialty: The Hungarian pointer/retriever nicknamed the 'Velcro dog' because it bonds intensely and remains physically attached to its owner's side.
Vizsla.care_notes: Requires significant physical endurance exercise daily; develops separation anxiety if left isolated for long stretches.

Walker Hound.physical_traits: Clean, muscular frame, smooth tricolor coat, high-held tail, clear expressive hound eyes.
Walker Hound.specialty: The Treeing Walker Coonhound is renowned for its blazing trailing speed and ability to tree quarry with a distinctive ringing chop/bay.
Walker Hound.care_notes: High tracking drive; cannot be trusted off-leash in open areas where it might pick up wild scent trails.

Weimaraner.physical_traits: Striking silver-gray coat, light amber or blue-gray eyes, tall sleek aristocratic frame.
Weimaraner.specialty: The 'Gray Ghost'; bred by the Court of Weimar to hunt big game (bears, cougars, deer); runs with high speed and endurance.
Weimaraner.care_notes: Can become neurotic and destructive without heavy exercise; strong predatory drive toward smaller household animals.

Welsh Springer Spaniel.temperament: Devoted, lively, affectionate, reserved with strangers
Welsh Springer Spaniel.physical_traits: Distinctive rich red-and-white coat, smaller vine-leaf shaped ears, compact athletic build.
Welsh Springer Spaniel.specialty: Ancient gundog bred to flush woodcock and waterfowl across Welsh bogs; handles freezing water and dense brambles.
Welsh Springer Spaniel.care_notes: More reserved than the English Springer; requires consistent, kind, positive-reinforcement training.

West Highland White Terrier.physical_traits: Harsh pure white double coat, dark button eyes and nose, carrot-shaped tail carried erect.
West Highland White Terrier.specialty: Bred in Poltalloch, Scotland, to hunt badgers and otters; pure white coat was selected so hunters wouldn't mistake the dog for prey.
West Highland White Terrier.care_notes: Prone to atopic dermatitis and skin allergies; coat requires hand-stripping or regular scissoring.

Whippet.physical_traits: Lean, aerodynamic frame, deep chest, narrow waist, fine short coat in various colors.
Whippet.specialty: Nicknamed 'the poor man's racehorse'; capable of reaching speeds up to 35 mph in seconds, followed by hours of sleeping on the couch.
Whippet.care_notes: Very low body fat makes them cold-sensitive; requires soft bedding to prevent pressure sores on joints.

Wire-Haired Fox Terrier.physical_traits: Dense, wiry, twisted coat in white with black and tan markings; folded V-shaped ears, erect tail.
Wire-Haired Fox Terrier.specialty: Engineered to flush foxes that went to ground during traditional British hunts; famous show champion with distinctive chiseled looks.
Wire-Haired Fox Terrier.care_notes: Will challenge other dogs regardless of size; requires hand-stripping to keep the coat harsh and colors vibrant.

Yorkshire Terrier.physical_traits: Floor-length, fine, silky blue-and-gold coat, compact square frame, erect V-shaped ears.
Yorkshire Terrier.specialty: Developed by Scottish weavers in Yorkshire textile mills to catch rats in tight machinery spaces before becoming a Victorian luxury pet.
Yorkshire Terrier.care_notes: Prone to dental decay and collapsed trachea; show coat requires daily wrapping and brushing, or a low-maintenance puppy cut.
